The paper proves that, for a certain class of Lagrangians, the associated quotient Aubry set is totally disconnected. In this context, the quotient Aubry set is obtained by identifying points in the Aubry set according to the natural equivalence relation arising in weak KAM theory. The main result states that this quotient space has no nontrivial connected components.

Total disconnectedness means that every connected component of the quotient Aubry set consists of exactly one point. In other words, the quotient Aubry set cannot contain any connected subset with more than one element. This property gives important information about the fine topological structure of the Aubry set and the way its static classes are arranged.

The paper also examines the significance of this result for Hamilton-Jacobi equations. In weak KAM theory, Aubry sets play a central role in understanding critical solutions and subsolutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations. The structure of the quotient Aubry set is closely related to questions of uniqueness and regularity for these equations, especially at the critical value. By proving total disconnectedness, the paper provides a useful topological insight into the behavior of critical subsolutions and their associated dynamics.

In addition, the paper discusses a Morse-Sard type property for differences of critical subsolutions. Classically, the Morse-Sard theorem concerns the set of critical values of smooth functions. In this setting, an analogous idea is applied to differences between critical subsolutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations. The paper investigates how the values taken by such differences on relevant critical sets behave, and how this behavior is connected to the topology of the quotient Aubry set. This perspective helps link variational methods, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, and geometric properties of the Aubry set.

The paper investigates the structure of the quotient Aubry set associated with a class of Lagrangian dynamical systems. In weak KAM theory and Hamilton-Jacobi dynamics, the Aubry set plays a central role because it contains the most dynamically significant invariant orbits and encodes important information about minimizing trajectories. However, its quotient by the natural equivalence relation induced by the Peierls barrier can be difficult to understand, and its topological structure is often subtle.

The main idea of the paper is to relate the quotient Aubry set to regularity and critical-value properties of differences of critical subsolutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations. These subsolutions arise naturally in the study of Hamiltonian systems and weak KAM theory. By using results of Morse-Sard type, the authors show that the values taken by certain differences of critical subsolutions have strong restrictions. This connection allows them to control the possible connected subsets of the quotient Aubry set.

The principal result is that, under the assumptions considered in the paper, the quotient Aubry set is totally disconnected. In other words, every connected component of the quotient Aubry set consists of a single point. This means that the quotient Aubry set contains no nontrivial connected continua, so its topology is highly fragmented. The theorem gives a precise description of the global structure of these quotient spaces and improves the understanding of how minimizing dynamics are organized.

This result is significant because Aubry sets and their quotients appear in many questions concerning Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics, viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations, and weak KAM theory. Showing that the quotient Aubry set is totally disconnected provides a clearer picture of the possible complexity of these objects and links their dynamical properties to analytic properties of Hamilton-Jacobi subsolutions.

Aubry’s ideas have had a lasting influence on the study of dynamical systems, especially in areas connected with variational principles and Hamiltonian mechanics. In this context, Lagrangians play a central role because they describe the behavior of a system through the difference between kinetic and potential energy. By analyzing the action associated with Lagrangians, one can understand the paths that a system naturally follows and identify special minimizing trajectories.

Moreover, Aubry’s work helped inspire what is now known as Aubry-Mather theory, which studies the structure of minimizing orbits in twist maps and related systems. This theory reveals that even in complex or chaotic dynamics, there may exist ordered sets of motions governed by deep mathematical principles. As a result, the study of Aubry sets and Lagrangians continues to be important in modern research, linking geometry, analysis, and dynamical systems.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract for a math paper proving that the quotient Aubry set for certain Lagrangians is totally disconnected and relating this to a Morse-Sard property for differences of critical Hamilton-Jacobi subsolutions.
counterfactuals.output: We prove that the quotient Aubry set associated with a broad class of Tonelli Lagrangians is totally disconnected. The argument is based on a Morse–Sard type property for differences of critical Hamilton–Jacobi subsolutions: if two such subsolutions coincide on the projected Aubry set, then the set of their critical values has empty interior in the appropriate quotient. This fine regularity property yields a separation mechanism for static classes and implies that the quotient Aubry set contains no nontrivial connected subsets. The result provides a new link between weak KAM theory, the structure of static classes, and nonsmooth Morse–Sard phenomena for critical subsolutions.
